subject: Recap and asks: DPA roles, logging SLA, and data residency — HealthBridge pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@healthbridge.com>, Legal - HealthBridge <legal@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap and asks: DPA roles, logging SLA, and data residency — HealthBridge pilot

Hi Daniel / HealthBridge legal — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups so we can get the pilot paperwork in motion. Attached: our current DPA (redwood_dpa_v3.pdf) and a tiny sample of audit logs we discussed (audit-logs-sample.csv).

Key clarifying questions from our side and asks from yours: 
- Controller / Processor: please confirm HealthBridge expects Redwood to be listed as a Processor under your DPA (we believe yes based on use-case but want explicit confirmation).
- Subprocessor disclosure: you asked for a current subprocessor list and evidence (SOC2). We can provide an export of the current subprocessors and our SOC2 report; let us know preferred delivery method (secure link vs. NDA'd bundle).
- Breach notification timing: you mentioned wanting faster notification. What is your preferred initial notice window (24h / 48h)? Our standard practice: high-level alert as soon as we have credible indicators (we can commit to an initial alert within 24h for high-severity incidents with an interim timeline and a full report within 72h after investigation). Confirm if that is acceptable.
- Retention / logs: clarification on retention for application logs vs. raw token-level logs. Our hosted product defaults to 90 days; Dedicated/Private options can extend retention. What is HealthBridges minimum retention requirement for the pilot (90d / 1yr / 7yr)?
- Data residency: you noted EU-only residency for some customers. We can enable region-specific hosting (EU region) for production and for Dedicated. For the pilot we can run a scoping test in the EU region; is that sufficient for now?
- Evidence access: you asked whether HealthBridge can request a one-time export of raw logs for auditing. We can do exports with sanitization/pseudonymization in most cases; need to align on format and scope.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Daniel / Legal to confirm controller/processor role and preferred breach window.
2) We will deliver: current subprocessor list + SOC2 link, sanitized sample logs, and a tracked DPA with proposed language for notify windows. (attached: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf)
3) Schedule a short security deep-dive (30-45m) next week to review logging format and residency options. Im proposing Thu May 25 10:00am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks — Ill loop in Monica (privacy counsel) and Marcus (solutions) on the follow-up thread.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
+aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap and asks: DPA roles, logging SLA, and data residency — HealthBridge pilot

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear notes and for sending the DPA. A few items from Legal and Security: 

1) Controller / Processor: HealthBridge will be Controller; Redwood will act as Processor. Please reflect that explicitly in the addendum.

2) Subprocessors / SOC2: we need a list of current subprocessors and a copy of your latest SOC2 Type II. Wed prefer the SOC2 delivered as a secure link (or uploaded to our SFTP) rather than an email attachment.

3) Breach notification: HealthBridges policy asks for initial notification within 24 hours of detecting an event that could reasonably affect patient data, with a fuller preliminary assessment within 48 hours and a complete root-cause report within 14 days. Would Redwood accept an initial notice + 48h preliminary and full report in 14d? If not, please propose exact timing.

4) Retention: for the pilot we need the option to retain logs for up to 3 years for auditability of specific workflows. We understand longer retention has cost implications — what are Redwoods configurable retention tiers and pricing implications?

5) Data residency: HealthBridge needs EU-only storage for EU-subject records. Is EU region support available immediately for pilot or only for Dedicated/Private? Wed like the pilot to mirror production residency.

6) Export of logs: for an audit we may request a one-time export of raw events (pseudonymized where required). Please confirm format (CSV/JSON) and any redaction options.

Finally, Legal asked whether Redwood will accept a small edit in the DPA concerning the notify window and an addendum clause limiting Redwoods liability to direct damages except in cases of willful misconduct. Please let us know whether Redwood legal can accept or counter.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — were targeting procurement sign-off by end-of-June if items are resolved.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Platform Partnerships | HealthBridge
Daniel.cho@healthbridge.com

Subject: Fwd: Recap and asks: DPA roles, logging SLA, and data residency — HealthBridge pilot

Team — forwarding HealthBridges response and a strawman for how we can respond. Key points they want: 24h initial notice, 48h preliminary assessment, 14d full report; 3-year retention option for logs; EU-only residency for EU data. Legal also asked about liability carveouts.

My proposed positions: 
- Controller/Processor: we accept Processor role for Redwood as long as scope is limited to data they send for inference. I think we can sign DPA as Processor.
- Subprocessors + SOC2: provide SOC2 Type II link and current subprocessor list. Marcus to prepare list & evidence export.
- Breach notify: offer initial alert within 24h for high-severity incidents, preliminary assessment within 48h, and a full report within 72h for confirmed incidents. Note: 14d full RCA is long; wed prefer 72h with a follow-up plan, but Legal may push for 14d. Monica: do we have flexibility to accept 14d for certain classes?
- Retention: our standard Hosted retention is 90d. For Dedicated/Private we can offer configurable retention up to 730 days (2 years) as part of pilot terms; 3 years would be possible as a custom contract with added storage fee. Marcus: can you run a quick estimate for cost delta for 3y?
- Data residency: EU region is available for Hosted EU and for Dedicated; however, Hosted EU is limited in some features (well confirm). For strict EU-only residency in production, Dedicated or Private is recommended. Laura: can we document the differences in a one-pager for Daniel?

Suggested reply to Daniel: confirm Processor role, share SOC2 link and subprocessor list, offer sanitized sample logs, propose initial notification within 24h + preliminary 48h + full report within 72h (but indicate we can accept 14d with exceptions) and present retention tiers (90d / 2y / custom). Ask for procurement timeline.

Action items: 
- Marcus: subprocessor list + SOC2 link (ETA EOD Wed 5/22)
- Monica: confirm whether Redwood legal will accept 14d full-report ask or whether 72h is hard limit (ETA EOD Wed 5/22)
- Laura: EU residency one-pager and feature differences (ETA Thu 5/24)

Ill incorporate your responses into a tracked DPA reply and send to HealthBridge.

Thanks,
Aisha

Hi Daniel / HealthBridge team — thanks for the detailed questions. Below is our summary response and proposed positions; where applicable weve noted follow-up docs were attaching.

Confirmations / proposals:
- Controller / Processor: Redwood will be listed as Processor under the addendum, scoped to processing of inputs submitted by HealthBridge for inference and associated logs.
- Subprocessors / SOC2: attached is a secure link to our SOC2 Type II (redwood_socs2_2028.pdf). Weve also attached the current subprocessor list in the draft reply (see attachments). Delivery method: secure link + Drive share (link sent to Legal thread).
- Breach notification: Redwoods proposed cadence: initial high-level notification within 24 hours of credible detection; preliminary assessment within 48 hours; full technical report and remediation plan within 72 hours for confirmed incidents. For exceptional, complex investigations we can agree milestones (e.g., 14d RCA) by exception; Monica (privacy counsel) will include language in the DPA addendum that provides that flexibility for complex investigations.
- Retention: Hosted default = 90 days. For pilot we can enable a 2-year retention tier on Dedicated; 3-year retention is supported as a paid customization. Marcus will include estimated delta in the commercial term sheet.
- Data residency: EU region hosting is available for the pilot if you opt for Hosted EU (feature parity caveat) or Dedicated (recommended for strict EU-only production). Laura attached a one-pager outlining the differences and feature caveats.
- Log exports: we can produce pseudonymized/raw event exports in CSV or JSON. Please indicate preferred format and the specific fields you require.
- Liability / DPA edits: Redwood legal prefers liability limited to direct damages with standard carve-outs; Monica will propose precise language in the tracked DPA were sending. Expect a redlined DPA (redwood_dpa_v3_redline.pdf) by EOD Thu.

Next steps / scheduling:
1) We will share: SOC2 link, subprocessor list, sanitized sample logs, and a redlined DPA by EOD Thu 5/23.
2) Proposed security deep-dive: Thu May 25 at 10:00am PT. Please confirm and well send a calendar invite with a brief agenda (logging format, residency, retention scenarios).
3) Marcus to follow up on retention pricing and operational impact.

If that all looks OK, well move forward to procurement and aim for a pilot start in early June.

Thanks again — looping in Marcus, Monica, and Laura on the thread.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
